reviews.reason: Correctly states that trust in an apparently exhaustive index suppresses fallback search and hides omitted content.
Faithfully captures why an incomplete authoritative index is more dangerous than having no index.
Accurately contrasts stale-index search suppression with the current-content search fallback triggered by an index's absence.
Correctly generalizes the mechanism from indexes to other authoritative artifacts such as stale specs, plans, and curated lists.
Faithfully includes both the generalized mechanism and the limitation that deterministic checks catch declared membership missing from an index, not undeclared semantic membership.
